findings.text: declaring a project's checks is no longer a swallowing read: the deleted recovery_review_subject.project_declares_review_checks caught pydantic's ValidationError and answered False, so a project whose domain block the schema rejects used to read as owing nothing, while domain_rules._domain_config raises. The caller is the review-record refusal path (reckon/crew/reports.py:1900 audits every stored record, reckon/crew_run_commands.py:853 runs 'crew check --review'), which is the read path _manifest_field_lines:2037 describes as not being allowed to fail a review, so a block edited into an invalid shape after the fact now aborts those readers with a traceback instead of reporting. The commit body and the fragment both disclose the direction as deliberate, and rules_for already raised for the node-bearing path, so this is recorded rather than repaired.

the manifest fallback's new assertion at :359 holds on both the old and the new reader, because the field the test writes is the unindented edge `orientation_write_paths: ["models/tape.py"]`, the shape the deleted line-prefix scanner also parsed. The change this round makes — routing through _manifest_field_lines so a field is read the way the rest of the contract reads it — therefore has no assertion that reddens if it is reverted: the block form _manifest_field_lines exists to handle (an empty value with the list indented beneath its key) is not exercised, and the worker's own fragment records that the test "carries no evidence that the routing changed". A case writing the indented shape would make it a discriminator.
